status: FORENSIC - no code modified in this section
full_path: Ollama /api/generate (raw text-completion endpoint, NOT /api/chat's role-structured messages API)
no_intermediate_transformation: RAGService passes retrieval_results straight through to LLMGenerator.generate(), which passes it straight through to build_prompt() with no filtering

A_where_text_enters_prompt.detail: result.text is the raw, verbatim chunk text, f-string-interpolated directly. No escaping, no filtering.

B_delimitation.detail: Plain-text heading '[Context N - <source label>]' + newline + raw text; chunks joined with double newline; section wrapped by '=== Context ===' / '=== Conversation History ===' headers. These are ordinary text strings, not a structurally distinct boundary - a chunk containing the literal string '=== Current Question ===' would be visually indistinguishable from the real section transition.

C_metadata_mixed_with_text.detail: Provenance heading sits immediately adjacent to raw chunk text, only a newline apart, no separate channel. Heading fields (video_title, document_title) derive in part from user-supplied filenames/video titles at ingestion - a theoretical secondary injection surface never tested in Phase 5E (which only injected via chunk body text).

D_role_markers_and_instructions_in_chunk.evidence: SPOOF-2/3/4 (Phase 5E) embedded literal User:/Assistant:/SYSTEM: line-prefixed text with zero filtering. SPOOF-5/6/7 embedded plain imperative instructions with NO role marker at all and succeeded or partially succeeded.

E_structure_resembling_trusted_instructi.core_gap: Ollama called via /api/generate with the entire prompt collapsed into one flat string - no API-level role separation. Ollama's /api/chat endpoint exists and accepts a messages array with role:system/user/assistant, using special template tokens plain text inside a message's content cannot forge. This project uses none of that - system instructions, Context, History, and Question are all adjacent regions of one plain-text blob distinguished only by informal '===' headers with no special status to the model.

F_history_vs_context_boundary.detail: Different header text but same weak, forgeable, plain-text mechanism as B. Not directly exploited in Phase 5E (which injected fake role-turns inside a Context chunk, not a forged '=== Conversation History ===' heading itself) - untested extension of the same attack surface, added to the Phase 5F-C threat model.

G_citations_metadata_same_channel.detail: Yes structurally (see C), though metadata fields are system/ingestion-controlled in Phase 5E's tests, not directly attacker-supplied.

I_existing_injection_tests.method: Targeted grep of tests/test_llm_generator.py - no test asserts injection resistance, role-marker handling, or instruction-override resistance

key_structural_observation: The Phase 5E payloads that actually succeeded (SPOOF-5, SPOOF-6, SPOOF-7) used NO role-marker prefixes at all - they were plain imperative sentences. A defense that only pattern-matches role-marker strings (SYSTEM:/USER:/ASSISTANT:) would catch the already-resisted cases (SPOOF-1-4) and miss the actually successful ones. The real gap is structural: no signal distinguishes 'trusted instruction' from 'untrusted data' anywhere in the flat prompt, so any sufficiently direct, confidently-phrased imperative sentence has an equal chance of being obeyed regardless of section. The smallest defensible fix must address this structural gap directly (strong, explicit, repeated untrusted-data framing bracketing the Context block), not rely on a keyword/pattern blocklist as the primary mechanism.
